input.source: user-provided lawful dump, kept outside git

X0.note: User-provided external retail XEX hash and title identity verified; no game binary or assets are tracked

X1.note: SDK v0.10.0 is pinned; eighteen live-memory-derived function entries have focused static regressions. ReXGlue codegen and Linux AMD64 build now accept the 68-byte 0x82341198 dispatcher; its runtime execution and the broader PPC/import/lowering report remain open.

X2.note: The plugin-enabled Linux AMD64 probe verified the retail VdEnableRingBufferRPtrWriteBack call with physical address 0x17AF403C and block-size log2 6. The GPU worker advanced the big-endian readback at descriptor+0x3C through values 25, 49, and 73; exact-XEX helper 0x823B2920 reads that +0x3C field. Earlier pristine probes watched the distinct descriptor+0x00 word, object+0x2ABD predicate, current KTHREAD+0x58 and object+13432; helper 0x823B33A0 was not entered, and the timeout helper 0x823BA9C8 traps when object+13432 is null. The 2026-10-24 exact-XEX Linux/GDB follow-up confirms source-0 retail callback 0x823B37B8 and 3,231 writes toggling the watched predicate byte between 0x04 and 0x14 via 0x823A4E48/0x823A4908. A separate 20-second Linux/GDB run with the recorded host executable/runtime/plugin hashes logged at least three source-0 callbacks entering 0x823A4640. Four sampled deferred-handler entries had queue read/write indexes 0/0 and a zero first record. Six sampled software-queue helper entries observed predicate values 0x00 then 0x14; retail predicate 0x823A0310 tests mask 0x02, clear in those samples. A new controlled Linux/GDB run sampled twelve source-0 callbacks and twelve consumer entries on object 0xB7365F00; every sampled read/write index remained 0/0, while candidate queue writer 0x823A4758 had no breakpoint hits. The observed callback stack originates in ReXGlue's SetupGuestGpu interrupt-dispatch lambda. This narrows the missing event to queue production/registration; it does not identify the cause or prove frontend progress. A separate retail GDB trace saw two calls to IoDismountVolumeByFileHandle with handle 0xF800003C from 0x827061E0; its caller ignores the return and continues to NtClose, and the same run proceeded to guest PM4/Vulkan submission. This does not establish the API's general unmount semantics. The earlier retained Linux log and descriptor+0 watch did not establish the EVENT_WRITE_SHD destination; a later plugin-enabled run (evidence/xbox360_event_write_ring_head_20261024.json) records per-packet writes to guest destination 0x17AF4000 and head-word progression 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 0xB, 0xD, 0xF, corresponding to the previously identified descriptor backing at 0xB7AF4000. This resolves the destination observation but not software-queue completion or the missing predicate bit 0x02 producer. A controlled SDL/uinput run (evidence/xbox360_linux_xam_input_routing_20261024.json) confirms Start and A states reach retail XamInputGetState user 0; inputs did not advance the frontend. The guest wait cause and menu progress remain open. Before the latest controlled launches, unused ReXGlue xenia_memory_* shared-memory objects consumed 4.7 GiB of /dev/shm; unreferenced current-user objects were removed before subsequent runs. In the exact 30-second run, two relative shader-cache directory opens failed with no VFS device 205 ms after the first readback; they do not explain that first black frame, and later shader-cache effects remain unknown. The 60-second exact Linux/GDB follow-up sampled 27 entries of retail helper 0x823B33A0 through call index 1500: software queue tail object+0x2A9C rose from 3 to 3003, while global 0x831B3820 remained 0 and the 1,624 observed predicate-byte writes were only 0x04/0x14. Static XEX code sets mask 0x02 only when VdIsHSIOTrainingSucceeded reports false; both the pinned ReXGlue stub and upstream Xenia return success (1), so this is expected retail gating and should not be forced. The separate software-queue consumer/head and predicate-bit 0x02 producer remain unresolved. A new 45-second exact-XEX Linux/GDB probe confirms startup registers callback 0x82649B68 on object 0xB7365F00 through 0x823A5730; the full retail leaf setter at 0x823A5730 stores r4 to r3+0x409C, matching the deferred producer callback slot. This identifies the stored field for those observed setter arguments but does not establish a producer hit or callback invocation. Source-0 interrupt delivery enters 0x823A4640, where eight sampled queue read/write index pairs remain 0/0. Candidate producer 0x823A4758 and the registered callback body were not hit. The producer and callback remain dynamically unobserved; frontend progress is unresolved. Static disassembly of 0x823B37B8 shows its source-0 branch calls 0x823A4640 only when separate address 0x7FC86544 has bit 0 set; this gate is distinct from object+0x2ABD bit 0x02 and global 0x831B3820. A new independent 60-second exact-XEX Linux/GDB trace on the current selected plugin artifact (SHA-256 ed4f4bf8cba7cd73efba45ab07edec96f6173e40007d5aa1b9fb188b7bcc252d) records 3,207 source-0 entries into 0x823B37B8 and 2,746 calls to deferred consumer 0x823A4640 from guest LR 0x823B3844. This updates the earlier no-source-0 observation: the retail MMIO gate path is now taken. The sampled deferred indices stay 0/0, predicate values are 0x00/0x04/0x14 with mask 0x02 clear, and candidate producer 0x823A4758 has zero hits. The wait remains active; this does not justify fabricating the predicate or patching guest semantics. A fresh 45-second read-only GDB trace on 2026-10-25, with the exact mapped plugin SHA badeb5c4052776fafca38fd265ff8c4c6091d1165ccd1da1a1bd385587a60637, reached source-0 hit counter 411 and deferred-consumer counter 380. Software queue head/tail samples advanced 1..129/3..131, while deferred queue indices remained 0/0, global 0x831B3820 remained 0, and sampled predicate values 0x00/0x04/0x14 never set mask 0x02. Producer 0x823A4758 and callback 0x82649B68 had no hits. This reproduces the queue frontier with mapped-plugin identity but does not identify the missing producer condition.

X3.note: Process 2 Linux evidence reports 1,828 retail PM4 packets, two guest swaps, 48 submitted retail point-list draws, and two Vulkan frame submissions. The exact-XEX Linux/GDB run recorded 161 draw submit entries and 161 accepted source-0/sample-0 Copy/Convert entries, but the retail 1280x720 A2B10G10R10 readback has zero non-black RGB pixels (FNV-1a B161DE6EEC272325). After clearing stale ReXGlue shared-memory objects, a fresh direct Linux run reproduced the same black retail readback. A separate magenta fragment-output diagnostic produced 518,400 non-black pixels (FNV-1a DA74DA070BC0D725), confirming the diagnostic raster/presenter/readback path; it is synthetic and not retail parity. Later 3-draw batches still fail the target/scissor match against PM4_XE_SWAP. Android readback is also black. At that time, visible retail output and scene parity remained unverified; the frame-specific follow-up below records the first original splash pixels. A 30-second Linux rerun with the exact host executable from the locked P1 evidence and Process 2 PR #2161 commit 8541089b produced byte-identical black readback (FNV-1a B161DE6EEC272325); repeated 3-draw batches still reject the target/scissor match. With that exact executable/plugin pair, a synthetic magenta control read back 518,400 nonblack pixels and had no 3-draw target/scissor rejection; this confirms diagnostic draw/presenter/readback coverage only, not retail parity. A later 60-second run using P2 diagnostic plugin SHA 54348dd521b97b15be963d0b9f680172dbfb83c3ef5f2fbb979f618dc9c32aaa with debug logging and no input recorded 3,010 three-draw refresh failures. The first was draw 1 sample count 1 versus frame sample count 4; both reported surfaces share color base 0, depth base 720, color format 1, and 1280x720 extent, while pitch differs (640 for draw 0, 1280 for draw 1). No shader/resource readiness diagnostic tokens appeared before this rejection, and the raw readback remains all black. This identifies the first rejection gate for this plugin build; it does not establish the correct pitch, shader translation, frontend output, or race progress. A 30-second Linux smoke using P2 plugin SHA-256 e05ea50726caea536e25f0e3f76d052e56740bdc455fb26d0884ecab8e8adfdd emitted no unresolved diagnostics for draws 27 or 28; draw 27's prior viewport/scissor rejection is absent, and batches of five indexed draws were submitted. Only draws 0 (incomplete raster state) and 29 (unsupported target/raster state) remained unresolved. The log has 1,762 presenter submission entries and no refresh failure, but no pixel readback was captured, so visible retail output remains unverified. A new 30-second Linux smoke with Process 2 plugin SHA-256 331794ec66bb3738aa3fae2c862952aa86283267c4a2b372736e5e813d42b892 emitted no unresolved-draw diagnostics for #27/#28, while #0 remained incomplete and #25/#29 remained unsupported. It logged 1,349 presenter submission entries (1,715 reported draw packets) and one guest swap-counter increment. The first 1280x720 VK_FORMAT_A2B10G10R10_UNORM_PACK32 readback is all black (0 non-black pixels; FNV-1a B161DE6EEC272325). This confirms the current first presenter output is still black; later-frame retail parity remains unverified. A 2026-10-24 Linux capture from the exact retail XEX now verifies the original SHIFT logo/loading splash in presenter submission 10 (54,748 non-black pixels; raw SHA-256 d6c09658bc16cd14056dc605fe2300becc540f0fca77a3d3e69dfae0d52f5824). A separate submission-200 capture is entirely black (SHA-256 cd6226f8bf299d3ab51cfc10af0b585167106d7caa356e8604bfe48ad9a49de5), but used a different plugin binary, so sustained output and the cause of the difference are unresolved. A later exact-XEX frame-10 readback using selected plugin artifact SHA-256 ed4f4bf8cba7cd73efba45ab07edec96f6173e40007d5aa1b9fb188b7bcc252d is black (zero nonblack RGB pixels; SHA-256 cd6226f8bf299d3ab51cfc10af0b585167106d7caa356e8604bfe48ad9a49de5). Process 2 diagnosed that plugin run as rejecting retail sampler anisotropy=3; visible output must be rechecked after that device-feature request is enabled. This is a different plugin artifact from the earlier splash capture and does not supersede its recorded pixels. A new exact-XEX Linux AMD64 run on 2026-10-24T21:46:10Z, using P2 plugin source 261ed976362d863286d3f065440cf67a5044d8a4 and SDK fix ede359f8a93cd26cb95531a0b39ed8584aa93bb7, captures presenter submission 10 with the original SHIFT logo/loading text/progress bar (59,101 non-black pixels). Its Vulkan validation log has zero VUID/Error entries while VK_EXT_swapchain_maintenance1 is enabled with its instance prerequisites. This confirms one retail splash readback, not sustained rendering or scene parity. A 60-second exact-XEX run on the newer P2 renderer source d57598912d173ebbc46f718c52dd36ae27826b06 captured submission 200 as opaque black (0 non-black RGB pixels); because the prior visible splash used a different plugin binary, this does not establish a splash-to-black transition. Current renderer logs still report missing vertex shader control register 0x2307 and an unsupported texture-fetch descriptor. A second run using the exact same host/runtime/plugin/XEX hashes as the submission-200 black readback reproduces the original logo/loading bar at submission 10 (59,101 non-black pixels). The captures are separate launches, not a continuous transition.

X4.note: The user confirmed that the original game loading screen appeared during an earlier ReXGlue Xbox run, but its exact process/build hash was not recorded. In the current controlled Linux run, callbacks and retail Vulkan submissions occur but the readback is entirely black. Four loose-file probes for menu_background.xml failed. The big-endian index of PakFiles/Menu_Background.bff is verified: 57 bounded members include menu_background.sgx/.enx and textures, but no menu_background.xml. The misses do not prove a fatal VFS problem or show whether the game opens this archive. The main menu and offline race remain unverified; the later exact-XEX Linux splash readback is recorded in evidence/xbox360_linux_retail_splash_readback_20261024.json. A controlled 2026-10-24 filtered uinput test confirms Start/A return through retail XamInputGetState for guest user 0, but these inputs did not advance the single-draw frontend. In the same retail run, four attempts to open menu_background.xml under the instances/static scene paths returned 0xc000000f; the archive index only proves Menu_Background.bff contains SGX/ENX and texture members, not the XML or fatality of the miss. The new independent 60-second GDB trace observes source-0 callbacks reaching the retail deferred consumer, but the software queue remains empty and its mask 0x02 predicate remains clear; the producer 0x823A4758 is not reached. This run still has no verified main menu or race. The new 2026-10-25 validation evidence records the same original splash readback; no main menu or offline race is demonstrated. The current plugin's submission-200 readback is opaque black; the earlier submission-10 splash came from another plugin build, so sustained frontend progress remains unverified. The mapped-plugin queue trace reproduces the source-0/deferred-consumer path without changing guest memory; its queue/predicate frontier remains open. With the same exact binaries as the separate submission-200 opaque-black run, submission 10 reproduces the original loading splash; no menu/race is shown, and the two runs do not establish a continuous transition.

X6.note: Source audit found a Vulkan 1.1 path but three optional feature bits are hard requirements; device feature probe and retail draw/present proof are pending. A Linux host run now verifies swapchain-maintenance extension activation with the required surface prerequisites and no validation VUIDs; Vulkan 1.1-only device compatibility remains unproven.
